info.title: Tangible
info.description: Self-hosted disc-image preservation, management, and burning.

get.description: List artifacts in creation order. Use `next_cursor` from the response to fetch the following page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum items to return. Clamped to [`MAX_LIMIT`].

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`.

get.description: Fetch one artifact with its components and any structural findings.
List the files making up an artifact.
Stream one component's bytes. Supports a single byte range, which is how a worker resumes an interrupted download.

416.description: The range lies outside the object

get.summary: The artifact's full manifest, exactly as stored.
get.description: Fetch the artifact manifest exactly as stored, byte for byte.

get.summary: One attempt, with the reports it produced.
get.description: Fetch one burn attempt, including the engine's write report and the read-back comparison when there is one.

post.summary: Record the end of an attempt.
post.description: Record the end of an attempt. Idempotent: retrying after a lost response returns the same physical copy rather than recording a second disc.

get.summary: The events recorded for one attempt, in sequence order.
get.description: List the events a worker reported for an attempt, in sequence order. Pass the response's `next_after` as `after` to continue.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return only events after this sequence.

post.summary: Submit worker events.
post.description: Submit worker events. Idempotent by sequence: resubmitting a batch already held changes nothing.

post.summary: Extend a lease.
post.description: Extend a lease. A refusal does not interrupt a write already in progress; it only prevents claiming more work.

get.description: List burn jobs, newest first. Filter by state, artifact, or disc; page with `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`.

post.summary: Queue a burn job.
post.description: Queue a burn job. Idempotent when an Idempotency-Key header is supplied: a repeat returns the first job rather than spending a second disc.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replay protection for a request that spends physical media

200.description: Already queued by an identical request

409.description: The key was used for a different request

422.description: The request will not be acted on

get.summary: One burn job, with every attempt made at it.
get.description: Fetch one burn job with its attempts. Each attempt past the first spent a disc.

get.summary: The attempts made at one job, oldest first.
get.description: List the attempts made at a burn job, oldest first.

post.summary: Cancel a burn job that has not started writing.
post.description: Cancel a burn job that has not started writing. Refused once a disc is being consumed, because stopping a write ruins the medium.

post.summary: Record that a person has accounted for a burn's disc.
post.description: Record that a person has accounted for a burn's disc. Releases a job stuck at needs_attention, leaving it failed so it can be retried.

409.description: This burn is not asking for attention

post.summary: Requeue a failed or cancelled job for another attempt.
post.description: Requeue a failed or cancelled burn job. Previous attempts are left as they are: a retry spends another disc and records another attempt.

409.description: Not in a state that can be retried

get.description: List the discs in a set, in order.

post.summary: Record a disc within a set.
post.description: Record one disc in a set. Disc numbers are unique within the set.

422.description: No such set, or an unusable value

get.description: Fetch one disc, the canonical object of this system.

post.summary: Link an artifact to the disc it represents.
post.description: Link an artifact to a disc, saying what it is to that disc. Linking again updates the claim rather than failing.

get.summary: The artifacts linked to a disc.
get.description: List the artifacts linked to a disc.

# Errors

`STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` if drives cannot be read.

post.summary: Ask for the disc in a drive to be erased.
post.description: Erase the rewritable disc in a drive, destroying everything on it. The request must set confirm_data_loss. The drive's worker takes it before any burn work, erases only a rewritable disc that holds data, and reports what it found.

409.description: The drive already has an erasure open

422.description: Not confirmed, or an unknown mode

get.summary: One edition, with its disc sets.
get.description: List the disc sets of an edition.

post.summary: Record a disc set within an edition.
post.description: Record what an edition shipped as.

422.description: No such edition, or an unusable name

get.description:
# Errors

`INVALID_PARAMETER` for a limit out of range.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many, at most 200. Defaults to 50.

get.description:
# Errors

`NOT_FOUND` for an unknown erasure.

post.summary: Withdraw an erasure the worker has not taken yet.
post.description: Withdraw a queued erasure. Refused once the drive has started: stopping an erase partway leaves the disc needing another one.

post.summary: Report how an erasure ended.
post.description: Report how an erasure ended. Repeating the same report is accepted.

422.description: An outcome or field that will not do

get.description: List the watched roots configured for importing, and the upload size limit.
List imports, newest first.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`.

post.summary: Import a file from a watched folder.
post.description: Import a file from a configured watched root. The server never accepts a host path: name a root and a relative path beneath it.

422.description: The path will not be resolved

post.summary: Upload a file and import it.
post.description: Upload a file as the request body and queue it for import. Streamed to disk as it arrives; the size limit is enforced on the bytes, not on a header.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Filename as it should be recorded. A detection hint, never a path.

get.description: Fetch one import, including how far it has got and any structural findings so far.

post.summary: Stop an import.
post.description: Stop an import. Honoured at any stage: nothing physical is consumed by importing.

post.summary: Try an import again.
post.description: Try a failed or cancelled import again, resuming from the last stage that completed.

get.summary: List the discs this system has produced.
get.description: List discs, newest first. Filter by catalog disc, artifact, or condition.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: disc_id
parameters.description: Only copies of this catalog disc.

get.summary: One disc, with every check recorded for it.
get.description: Fetch one disc and its check history, newest check first.

patch.summary: Record what an operator knows about a disc.
patch.description: Record a disc's label, whereabouts, notes or condition. Absent fields are left alone. `verified` cannot be set by hand: record a check.

post.summary: Record a check performed on a disc.
post.description: Record a check. The disc's condition follows what the check found: this is the only path to `verified`.

post.summary: Record that a disc has been destroyed.
post.description: Record that a disc has been destroyed. Irreversible: the record remains, but nothing further can be recorded against it.

post.summary: Sign in.
post.description: Sign in with a username and password. Sets the session cookie and returns the anti-forgery token mutations must send.

401.description: The username or password is wrong

429.description: Too many failures for this username

delete.description:
# Errors

`STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` if the session cannot be ended.

get.summary: Whether the server still needs its first account.
get.description:
# Errors

`STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` if accounts cannot be counted.

post.summary: Create the first administrator and sign them in.
post.description: Create the first account, an administrator, and sign it in. Works only while no account exists.

422.description: The username or password will not do

get.description: List titles in sort order. Pass `search` to filter by name and `next_after` from the response to continue.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Only titles whose name contains this.

post.summary: Record a title.
post.description: Record a work. Editions, disc sets and discs hang off it.

422.description: The request will not be stored

get.description: Fetch one title.
List the editions of a title.

post.summary: Record an edition of a title.
post.description: Record a particular release of a title.

422.description: No such title, or an unusable name

get.description:
# Errors

`STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` if accounts cannot be read.

post.summary: Create an account.

422.description: The username, password or role will not do

post.summary: Issue a one-use enrollment token for a new burn worker.
post.description: Issue a one-use enrollment token for a new burn worker. The token is returned once and cannot be recovered; it expires after 15 minutes unless asked otherwise, at most 60. Needs an administrator, and is audited.

400.description: The lifetime is out of range

post.summary: Exchange a one-use enrollment token for a worker credential.
post.description: Exchange a one-use enrollment token for a worker credential. The credential is returned once and cannot be recovered.

409.description: The name is already in use

put.summary: Record what a worker and its drive can do.
put.description: Report what this worker and its drive can do, and receive the drive identifier to claim work with.

422.description: The report will not be accepted

post.summary: Ask for work.
post.description: Ask for a burn job. Answers 204 when there is nothing to do.

post.summary: Ask for an erasure queued for this worker's drive.
post.description: Take the next erasure queued for this worker's drive. Answers 204 when there is none, or while a burn attempt holds the drive.

404.description: Not this worker, or not its drive

post.summary: Report that a worker is alive.
post.description: Report that a worker is alive and receive any instruction to stop taking new work.

post.summary: Reconcile a worker that restarted holding local state.
post.description: Reconcile a worker that restarted holding local state. No directive ever permits writing.

get.summary: Liveness probe: the process is running and the runtime is responsive.
get.description: Liveness. Answers whenever the process can serve a request and deliberately checks no dependency, so a database outage cannot cause a restart loop.

get.summary: Readiness probe: every dependency needed to serve traffic is usable.
get.description: Readiness. Answers 503 when any dependency is unusable so that traffic is withheld rather than sent into failure.

503.description: At least one dependency is down

components.description: The files making up the artifact.

oneOf.description:
The disc's tracks, when the artifact was described by a CUE sheet or a
TOC whose tracks could be laid out.

format_confidence.description: Detection confidence, from 0 to 1. Diagnostic only.

ArtifactDetail.description: Everything known about one artifact, short of its full manifest.

ArtifactSummary.description:
An artifact as it appears in a listing.

Deliberately not the whole manifest: a listing of a large library should
not carry every component of every artifact.

has_warnings.description:
Whether anything structural is worth an operator's attention.

Surfaced in the summary so a damaged artifact is visible in a list
without opening it.

source_filename.description: Filename as received, when one was recorded.

ArtifactSummaryPage.description:
A page of artifact summaries.

A concrete type rather than a generic instantiation so the published
OpenAPI names something a client generator can produce cleanly.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when this is the last.

verify_report.description: The read-back comparison, when one ran.

write_report.description: The engine's account of the write, once there is one.

BurnAttemptDetail.description: One attempt with the reports it produced.

BurnAttemptView.description: One execution of a burn job.

attempt_number.description: Which attempt this is, starting at 1.

consumed_media.description: Whether this attempt consumed a disc.

ended_at.description: When it ended, if it has.

error_code.description: A stable failure code, when it failed.

error_detail.description: Human-readable failure detail, when it failed.

last_event_sequence.description: Highest event sequence held for it.

physical_copy_id.description: The disc this attempt produced, if it produced one.

next_after.description:
Sequence to pass as `after` to continue, or null at the end.

A sequence rather than an opaque cursor: sequences are already the
currency of this timeline (the worker numbers events with them and
the server acknowledges them), so hiding them here would be a
different vocabulary for the same thing.

warnings.description:
Things worth knowing before the disc is spent.

Warnings, not refusals: an operator may knowingly burn an artifact
that validated with warnings, and the system's job is to say so rather
than to decide for them.

BurnJobCreated.description: A newly queued job, with anything an operator should know about it.

BurnJobDetail.description: A burn job with its attempts.

items.description: The jobs in this page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when this is the last.

attempt_count.description:
How many attempts have been made, including failed ones.

Each attempt past the first spent a disc, so this is not a retry
counter but a count of media consumed.

completed_at.description: When it finished, if it has.

eject_policy.description: What to do with the disc afterwards.

has_started_writing.description:
Whether a disc is being or has been consumed.

Derived from the state so a client does not have to know which states
those are. It is what decides whether cancelling is still offered.

priority.description: Queue priority; higher is claimed first.

oneOf.description: The most recent thing a worker reported, if any.

requested_media_profile.description: Media profile requested, when one was.

BurnProgress.description: What a worker last said it was doing.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code for the event.

fraction.description: Progress within that stage, from 0 to 1, when the stage reports it.

cache_free_bytes.description: Free bytes in its staging cache.

drive_id.description:
The drive's identifier, to be used when claiming work.

Assigned by the server rather than supplied: public identifiers are
the server's to issue, and a worker that could choose one could claim
another worker's drive.

CheckView.description: One check performed on a disc.

observed_sha256.description: The digest read back, when the method produces one.

ClaimRequest.description: What a worker offers when asking for work.

drive_id.description: The drive the work would run on.

engine.description: The engine the worker would use.

artifact.description: What to write, and where to fetch it.

attempt_id.description: The attempt created for this claim.

eject_policy.description: What to do with the disc when the attempt ends.

lease_token.description: The lease token, presented on subsequent requests for this attempt.

requested_media_profile.description:
Media profile the operator asked for, if any.

Advisory until claims filter on drive capability: a worker whose drive
cannot write this must fail preflight rather than write the wrong
medium.

ClaimedArtifact.description: Where a worker fetches what it is to write.

manifest_sha256.description:
Digest of the manifest as published, when the library is readable.

The worker checks what it downloads against this. It does not make the
manifest trustworthy (it came from the same server), but it catches a
document altered or truncated between publication and the download.

manifest_url.description:
Path to fetch the manifest from, relative to the server.

A path rather than an absolute URL: the worker already knows which
server it is talking to, and a server that told it otherwise would be
redirecting a staging download somewhere the operator never
configured.

CompletionRequest.description: What a worker sends when it finishes.

oneOf.description: Why it failed, when it did.

last_sequence.description: The last event sequence the worker emitted.

lease_token.description: The lease token from the claim.

oneOf.description: The read-back comparison, when one ran.

write_report.description: The engine's account of the write.

acknowledged.description: Always true when the server has the completion recorded.

physical_copy_id.description: The disc recorded, when the attempt consumed media.

CreateBurnJobRequest.description: What an operator sends to queue a burn.

eject_policy.description: What to do with the disc afterwards. Defaults to ejecting on success.

priority.description: Queue priority; higher is claimed first. Defaults to 0.

requested_media_profile.description: Media profile to require, or null for whatever fits.

verification_policy.description: Ordered verification steps. Defaults to a full read-back.

display_name.description: What it is called, when it has a name of its own.

media_family.description: What kind of medium it is. Defaults to unknown.

sequence_number.description: Which disc of the set it is. Starts at 1.

disc_count_expected.description: How many discs it should contain.

set_kind.description: What shape of set it is. Defaults to unknown.

region.description: Which region it was sold in.

CreateImportRequest.description: What an operator sends to import from a watched folder.

path_id.description: Which configured root the file is under.

relative_path.description: Where beneath that root, as a relative path.

kind.description: What kind of work it is. Defaults to unknown.

sort_title.description: What it sorts as. Defaults to the display title.

username.description: The username. Case does not matter.

detail.description:
Operator-facing failure summary. Never carries a connection string or
credential, only the error class.

DiscArtifactView.description: An artifact linked to a disc.

confidence.description: How confident the link is, from 0 to 1.

relationship.description: What the artifact is to the disc.

catalog.description: Media catalogue number, when the disc carries one.

DiscSetView.description: The discs an edition shipped as.

disc_count.description:
How many are catalogued.

Beside the expected count so an incomplete set is visible without
counting rows by eye.

disc_count_expected.description: How many discs it should contain.

set_kind.description: What shape of set it is.

artifact_count.description: How many artifacts are linked to it.

compatibility_claim.description:
What reproduction is expected to achieve.

`unknown` unless evidence has been recorded, which is the schema's own
rule: anything stronger must be backed by something.

copy_count.description: How many physical copies of it this system has made.

display_name.description: What it is called, when it has a name of its own.

media_family.description: What kind of medium it is.

sequence_number.description: Which disc of the set it is.

volume_label.description: The volume label read from an image of it.

DriveReportBody.description: What a worker says about one drive.

capabilities.description: What the drive says it can do.

device_alias.description:
Worker-local stable alias, such as `/dev/disc-block`.

Supplied by the worker and never a host device node. Together with the
worker it is the drive's identity, which is why the same alias
reported twice updates one drive rather than creating a second.

serial_hash.description:
SHA-256 of the drive serial, hashed by the worker.

Hashed before it is sent, so the raw serial never leaves the machine
that read it. The server only needs to recognise a drive, not to name
its hardware in an export.

DriveView.description: A drive, and the worker it belongs to.

device.description: Its device path inside the worker's container.

worker_last_seen_at.description: When the worker last reported in.

EditionView.description: A particular release of a title.

region.description: Which region it was sold in.

set_count.description: How many disc sets it has.

EngineReport.description: One engine a worker can run.

version.description: Its version, as the engine reports it.

EnrollmentRequest.description: What a worker sends to enroll.

enrollment_token.description: The one-use token an administrator issued.

name.description: A human-meaningful name for this worker.

EnrollmentResponse.description: What a newly enrolled worker receives.

credential.description: The credential, returned exactly once and never recoverable.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the server selected.

ErasureClaim.description: An erasure a worker has taken.

ErasureClaimRequest.description: What a worker sends to ask for an erasure.

ErasureCompletion.description: How an erasure ended, as the worker reports it.

duration_seconds.description: How long it took, in seconds.

error_code.description: A stable code saying why it did not erase.

oneOf.description: What was in the drive, when there was a disc to look at.

profile.description: The media profile the drive reported, such as `DVD-RW`.

ErasureView.description: A request to erase the disc in a drive, and how it went.

duration_seconds.description: How long the erase took, in seconds.

error_code.description: Why it did not erase, when it did not.

oneOf.description: What the worker found in the drive before deciding.

touched_the_disc.description:
Whether the disc may have been changed: true once an erase has run,
whatever it achieved.

accepted_through_sequence.description: The highest contiguous sequence held. The worker prunes against this.

EventSubmission.description: One event in a submitted batch.

FailureReport.description:
Why an attempt did not succeed.

Sent alongside the reports rather than inferred from them, because the
reports say *what* happened and this says why. Without it a failed burn
tells an operator only that it failed.

detail.description: Human-readable detail, bounded by the server before storage.

HeartbeatResponse.description: What the server tells a worker on each heartbeat.

drain.description: Whether the worker should stop taking new work.

server_time.description: The server's clock, so a worker can notice drift.

items.description: The imports in this page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when this is the last.

ImportSources.description: Where imports may be taken from.

max_upload_bytes.description: Largest upload the server will accept, in bytes.

watch_roots.description:
Identifiers of the watched roots an administrator configured.

Identifiers only. The paths behind them are the host's business and
are never exposed.

artifact_id.description: The artifact it produced, once it has.

bytes_expected.description: How many bytes are expected, when the source said.

completed_at.description: When it finished, if it has.

error_code.description: A stable failure code, when it failed.

error_detail.description: Human-readable failure detail, when it failed.

is_settled.description: Whether the import has finished, one way or another.

resumes_from.description:
Whether a retry would resume rather than start again.

Surfaced because it is the question an operator asks before pressing
retry on a large import.

source_filename.description: The filename as received, when one was recorded.

warnings.description:
Structural observations gathered so far.

Present as soon as inspection has run, so a warning is visible before
the import finishes rather than only afterwards.

IssueEnrollmentRequest.description:
What an operator sends to issue an enrollment token. Every field is
optional; `{}` asks for the defaults.

expires_in_minutes.description: Minutes until the token lapses, from 1 to 60. Defaults to 15.

enrollment_id.description: The enrollment's identifier, for the audit log and for revoking it.

enrollment_token.description:
The token. Returned this once and never again: the server keeps only
its hash.

LinkArtifactRequest.description: A link between an artifact and a disc.

confidence.description:
How confident the link is, from 0 to 1. Defaults to certain, because
an operator linking by hand is the strongest evidence there is.

relationship.description: What the artifact is to the disc. Defaults to a representation of it.

status.description: Always `"alive"` when the process can serve a request at all.

version.description: Server version, from the crate version at build time.

PhysicalCopyDetail.description: A disc with its check history.

items.description: The discs in this page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when this is the last.

check_count.description: How many checks have been recorded.

disc_id.description: The catalog disc this is a copy of.

is_settled.description: Whether anything further can be recorded about it.

label.description: What is written on the disc itself.

last_checked_at.description: When it was last read back.

manufacturer_id.description: Manufacturer identifier, when the drive reported one.

media_serial.description: Media serial, when the drive reported one.

should_be_destroyed.description:
Whether it should be taken out of circulation.

Derived from the condition so a client does not have to know which
conditions mean "bin this". It is the question an operator is really
asking when they look at a shelf.

verification_level.description: What verification ran when it was burned.

manufacturer_id.description: Manufacturer identifier, when the drive reported one.

serial.description: Media serial, when the drive reported one.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Clients branch on this, not on `detail`.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation. May be reworded between releases.

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body as the RFC allows.

type.description: A URI identifying the problem type.

checks.description: Per-dependency detail, so an operator can see *what* is failing.

status.description: `"ready"` when every dependency is usable, otherwise `"degraded"`.

method.description: What was done, from the verification vocabulary.

observed_sha256.description: The digest read back, when the method produces one.

RecoveryRequest.description: What a worker reports when it restarts holding local state.

attempt_id.description: The attempt the worker was running.

engine_process_state.description: Whether the engine process is still running.

last_event_sequence.description: The last event sequence it emitted.

local_stage.description: The stage the worker believes it reached.

directive.description: One of the protocol's recovery directives.

discard_local_state.description: Whether local state may be dropped.

may_accept_new_work.description: Whether the worker may take new work.

may_write.description: Always false. Restarting a write is never a recovery action.

RenewRequest.description: What a worker sends to renew.

lease_token.description: The lease token from the claim.

RequestErasure.description: What an operator sends to erase the disc in a drive.

confirm_data_loss.description:
Must be `true`. Erasing destroys everything on the disc in the drive,
and the request has to say that this is intended.

mode.description:
`quick`, which does only what makes the disc writable again, or
`full`, which writes over the whole disc. Quick is fast on a CD-RW;
some drives erase a whole DVD-RW either way, which takes half an hour
or more. Full can take an hour.

csrf_token.description:
The token every mutation must send in `X-CSRF-Token`.

Not a credential on its own: it is useless without the session
cookie, which a page's script cannot read.

expires_at.description: When the session ends however much it is used.

SetupStatus.description: Whether the server still needs its first account.

needed.description: True until the first administrator exists.

items.description: The titles in this page, in sort order.

next_after.description:
The sort key to pass as `after` to continue, or null at the end.

The sort title rather than an opaque cursor, because the ordering is
alphabetical and a client showing "continue from R" should be able to
say so.

kind.description: What kind of work it is.

number.description: Index number; 0 is the pregap, 1 the track proper.

relative_lba.description: Sectors from the track's first present sector.

TrackVerificationReport.description: The check on one track of a disc described as tracks.

check.description:
`byte_compare`, or `length_and_readable` for a track that was read back
and measured but not compared.

expected_sha256.description: The digest of what was written, for a byte comparison.

observed_sha256.description: The digest of what was read back, for a byte comparison.

sectors_expected.description: Sectors the layout says the track proper holds.

component_id.description: The component its bytes are in.

file_offset_bytes.description: Where in that component its first sector is.

indexes.description: Index points, relative to the first present sector.

mode.description: Mode, as a CUE sheet spells it: `AUDIO`, `MODE1/2048`, `MODE2/2352`.

pregap_sectors.description: Sectors of gap before index 1, generated and in the file together.

sample_byte_order.description:
How an audio track's samples are stored: `little_endian` or
`big_endian`.

start_lba.description: Its first present sector, counted from the start of the image.

UpdatePhysicalCopyRequest.description:
What an operator may change about a disc.

Every field is optional, and absent means "leave it alone", so a client
editing a label cannot blank a storage location it never saw.

label.description: What is written on the disc.

status.description:
Its condition.

`verified` and `verification_failed` are refused: those words describe
what a read-back found, and recording a check is how they are written.

UserView.description: An account, without anything that would sign anybody in.

disabled.description: Whether the account has been disabled.

VerificationReport.description: The read-back comparison, when one ran.

expected_sha256.description: The digest the artifact should have.

observed_sha256.description: The digest actually read from the disc.

tracks.description: What was checked on each track, for a disc described as tracks.

WriteReport.description: The engine's account of the write.

session_cookie.name: tangible_session
session_cookie.description: Set by signing in. Mutations must also send the session's anti-forgery token in X-CSRF-Token.

tags.name: catalog
tags.description: Titles, editions, disc sets, and discs

tags.name: burns
tags.description: Burn jobs, attempts, and their events
